citation: Cordero et al. (2022), MBSE Challenges in the Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats: Nanospace Study
title: MBSE Challenges in the Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats: Nanospace Study
venue_type: conference, IEEE SysCon inferred from DOI metadata; venue name not stated in paper text
modeling_scope: Preliminary CubeSat system/CDE model integrated with Nanospace: requirements and constraints, mission/orbit, telecommunications, energy and power, structure, budgets, dependency graph/DSM, SysML requirements/function/state/internal block/parametric diagrams, and simulation scripts for power, data, link, and reentry checks. EPS is covered as an energy/power budget and constraint-checking area, not as a standalone EPS behavioral model.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML model in an unnamed SysML tool; dependency graphs and design structure matrices; MB2DM to generate DSMs from SysML; Nanospace GUI/database/API; Python scripts using GMAT, Dosa, Stela, Celestlab for preliminary analyses. OPM and ARCADIA/Capella are mentioned as alternatives, not used in the experiment.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite platform; CREME CubeSat Radiation Environment Monitoring Experiment in LEO; paper explores 2U feasibility and then 3U design scenario with deployable solar arrays.
task_domain: Concurrent preliminary design of CubeSats, using the CREME radiation-monitoring CubeSat as a case study; mission/orbit, power, telecommunications, data, structural, and reentry trade-offs.
interface: Nanospace web GUI, database, and API for parameter storage, data sharing, third-party expert software exchange, and envisioned integration with an MBSE tool through API links to budgets, reports, DSMs, and parameter relations.
feedback: Dependency graph and DSM show feedback loops and indicate which script parts/design parameters must be rerun or updated after unmet requirements; simulations feed intermediate results back into Nanospace for team sharing.
evaluation: Demonstrated through the CREME simplified but real CubeSat use case, SysML/DSM experiment, and semi-automated Python/GMAT/Dosa/Stela/Celestlab analyses. Iterations check power DoD, data/link budget, and reentry constraints. No controlled performance comparison of Nanospace with versus without MBSE is reported; this is proposed as future work.
rq_relevance: RQ1 partial: the paper models CubeSat preliminary design at system level with requirements, budgets, dependencies, SysML, DSMs, and an energy/power budget, but it does not present a general EPS behavioral model with minimal prior knowledge. RQ2 partial: it claims MBSE/model integration benefits such as reuse, traceability, communication, consistency, faster convergence, and data/tool integration, but does not provide EPS-specific reliability or reproducibility evidence. RQ3 partial: it links MBSE to design/verification in general and shows pre-physical simulation checks for power DoD and other constraints, but it does not define explicit EPS verification procedures inside an MBSE model.
claimed_outcomes: MBSE may let Nanospace reuse knowledge, accelerate design convergence, and speed inspection of candidate architectures.
Claimed MBSE benefits include better communication/information sharing, increased traceability and reuse, reduced time and cost, improved consistency, system understanding, and systems design.
Nanospace supports direct information exchange between third-party expert software, transparent data visualization, concurrent data access, and sharing of intermediate results.
SysML-derived DSMs can provide change-propagation information, indicate unsatisfied requirements in the UI, and show which design parameters must be updated.
Reliability outcomes attributed to MBSE/EPS modeling: Not reported.
Reproducibility outcomes are not stated directly; the closest claimed outcomes are knowledge reuse, traceability, and archiving/reusing knowledge.
verification_validation_linkage: General MBSE definition and discussion link modeling to requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation. In the CREME case, simulations check requirements/constraints before physical development, including EPS-related battery depth-of-discharge/power feasibility, telecom data/link budget, and reentry. Nanospace UI can mark requirements as satisfied or not. No explicit EPS-specific verification procedure model or IVV workflow is reported.
key_findings: The paper frames Nanospace as an open-source web CDE environment for academic CubeSat preliminary design and examines early MBSE integration challenges.

CubeSat preliminary design is represented through requirements, constraints, subsystem parameters, budgets, dependency graphs, and DSMs across mission/orbit, telecom, onboard computing, energy and power, structure, payload, and ground segment.

In the CREME example, payload and platform estimates lead to power and communications constraints; a 2U scenario with four 4 W solar arrays violates the battery DoD constraint, while a 3U scenario with four 6 W arrays can recharge the battery in the shown simulation.
The 2000 km SSO scenario fails the 25-year reentry constraint, illustrating how DSM/dependency information guides which parameters need redesign.

A CubeSat SysML experiment used requirements diagrams, a state-machine functional diagram, internal block diagrams, and parametric diagrams for subsystems; DSMs can be generated from SysML models using MB2DM.
The paper identifies tool/data integration as a key challenge: different tools are used for different purposes, MBSE connectivity is not automatic, and information can be lost across tools.
Nanospace is presented as a facilitator for data storage and sharing, not an autonomous preliminary design tool; human expertise and external analysis tools remain required.
limitations_gaps: Only a subset of CREME requirements and constraints is considered because of space constraints.
Mission modes are not discussed, although the authors state the concept could be extended to include them.
ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations are excluded from the example, although described as modularly addable.
The process is semi-automatic and requires human expertise to avoid non-converging designs and make trade-offs.
The paper states that lack of data continuity across the lifecycle and coherence between tools is a major issue for CDE tools including Nanospace.
MBSE software connectivity does not come automatically, and model exchange can lose information.
Manual construction of dependency graphs is called counter-intuitive; further MB2DM integration and Nanospace database redesign are needed.
Comparison of Nanospace performance with and without an MBSE vision is proposed as future work, not performed.

quality.rationale: IEEE DOI/conference metadata indicates a credible conference venue. The paper explicitly discusses limitations and gaps including restricted scope, excluded mission modes/subsystems, semi-automation with human expertise, data continuity, tool connectivity, database redesign, and future comparative evaluation.

evidence_quotes.claim: Study focus on MBSE integration with Nanospace
evidence_quotes.quote: the early endeavours of the incorporation of a Model-based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approach to the open-source Nanospace framework is discussed

MBSE provides good benefits... better communication/information sharing, increased traceability and capacity for reuse, reduce time and cost, improved consistency, system understanding and systems design.
assess how the incorporation of a Model-based Systems Engineering approach to the concurrent preliminary design of CubeSats... can be realised

evidence_quotes.claim: Power criticality and battery DoD constraint
evidence_quotes.quote: without power, the CubeSat would basically become space debris... the battery's Depth of Discharge (DoD) must remain above a threshold

evidence_quotes.claim: MBSE captures dependencies and supports reuse/traceability
evidence_quotes.quote: MBSE can be used to capture the system dependencies represented in Figs.1 and 2, allowing to reuse knowledge from previous CubeSat missions.

evidence_quotes.claim: Nanospace API and semi-automated parameter updates
evidence_quotes.quote: Requirements... are set into Nanospace... They are automatically updated in the database through Nanospace API.
The dependency graph... or the design structure matrix... are available to show the feedback loops and sequence of which part of the script should be re-run.
Simulation allows for a first check on the order of magnitude of available power... the power input from the solar panels is insufficient... a violation of constraint C-06
Nanospace benefits from the change propagation information available from DSMs that for instance can be automatically generated from SysML models by the tool MB2DM.
Models are used to represent the system and enable to better master the design and the verification of complex systems.

a CubeSat model was realised in a SysML tool, creating requirements diagrams, realising a functional diagram using the state machine diagram, then an internal block diagram was used, as well as internal diagrams for each subsystem using the parametric diagram.
MBSE software connectivity does not come automatically and few models can be exchanged between software without information loss.

evidence_quotes.claim: Conclusion on MBSE effect in Nanospace
evidence_quotes.quote: MBSE system models could enhance the propagation of parameter updates or changes on Nanospace, whether using parametric design structure matrices or dependency graphs.

evidence_quotes.claim: Nanospace is not autonomous and needs external tools
evidence_quotes.quote: It cannot realise a preliminary design autonomously, but needs to work with other tools

notes_for_consistency: Read only paper.md. Venue name is not printed in the paper text; conference/IEEE SysCon is inferred from embedded DOI metadata.
